Boston, MA
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.
WHOOP is seeking a Vice President of Hardware Quality to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of quality across our global hardware ecosystem. This leader will be responsible for ensuring quality is embedded throughout the product lifecycle — from early product development through manufacturing, supplier management, and field performance. Working closely with Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Membership Services, Finance, and manufacturing partners, you will build scalable systems, drive operational excellence, and create a culture of continuous improvement that enables WHOOP to deliver exceptional products and member experiences at scale.
Responsibilities
Define and execute a comprehensive quality strategy spanning product quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, field quality, and containment across the hardware lifecycle.
Build, lead, and develop a world-class global quality organization that enables operational excellence and unlocks growth and scale.
Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Product Development teams to ensure robust quality planning, validation, and risk mitigation throughout new product introduction and sustaining engineering activities.
Establish quality metrics, operating mechanisms, and executive reporting frameworks that provide visibility into quality performance, risks, and opportunities across the supply chain.
Drive closed-loop quality improvement initiatives by connecting field performance, reliability testing, manufacturing data, supplier performance, and product design insights.
Lead supplier quality programs, including qualification processes, factory audits, corrective and preventive actions, and strategic supplier development efforts across a global manufacturing network.
Qualifications
10+ years of leadership experience in hardware quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or related functions supporting consumer electronics, wearable technology, or other complex hardware products.
Demonstrated success building and scaling high-performing quality organizations in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
Deep understanding of consumer electronics manufacturing processes, including electro-mechanical assemblies, PCB/SMT manufacturing, batteries, plastics, and critical component qualification.
Experience working with global manufacturing and supplier partners and managing quality across geographically distributed operations.
Expertise in quality systems and methodologies, including statistical process control, auditing, corrective and preventive action programs, root cause analysis, FMEA, Design for Manufacturing, Lean manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence decisions through data-driven insights and cross-functional partnership.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% internationally to support manufacturing partners, suppliers, and quality initiatives.
Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.
This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.

Summary
The Manufacturing Operations Leader will own and drive the performance of two key value streams within our aerospace and defense manufacturing environment. This leader will be responsible for delivering safe, high-quality, cost-effective products on schedule while developing a high-performing operations organization.
The ideal candidate is an experienced manufacturing leader with 5+ years of progressive experience in a people-leading role who can translate business objectives into disciplined operational execution. This role requires strong leadership, cross-functional collaboration, continuous improvement, and a deep commitment to quality and customer mission success.

Strive toward a culture of proactive safety.
Establish operational priorities, performance goals, and accountability across both value streams.
Develop and execute production plans to meet customer schedules and business objectives.
Monitor key performance indicators and drive corrective actions when targets are not achieved.
Partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Program Management, Human Resources, and other functions to resolve production issues.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and other operational excellence methodologies.
Identify and eliminate bottlenecks, waste, production constraints, and process inefficiencies.
Ensure compliance with aerospace and defense quality standards, company procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Support new product introduction, production ramp-up, process improvements, and manufacturing readiness activities.
Manage capacity, labor, equipment, and resource requirements across both value streams.
Lead root-cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions for recurring operational issues.
Develop and manage operating budgets while identifying opportunities to improve cost and productivity.
Establish effective visual management and daily operating rhythms to maintain focus on critical metrics.
Communicate operational performance, risks, and improvement plans to senior leadership.
Foster a collaborative environment focused on delivering reliable aerospace and defense products that support the warfighter.
Other duties as assigned.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management or related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive manufacturing or operations leadership experience, preferably within aerospace, defense, aviation, or another highly regulated industry.
Demonstrated experience leading multiple manufacturing teams, production areas, or value streams.
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, capacity management, and operational metrics.
Proven ability to lead through complex production challenges and deliver measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Strong knowledge of quality systems and manufacturing requirements applicable to aerospace and defense environments.
Demonstrated ability to develop and retain high-performing teams.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills.
Ability to effectively collaborate across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Program Management, and executive leadership.
Experience with ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing performance metrics.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities and demanding customer requirements.
Physical Requirements
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the work shift.
Ability to frequently use hands and fingers to operate machine controls, tools, and measuring instruments.
Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and components weighing up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and reach as required to load, unload, and inspect parts and equipment.
Ability to perform repetitive motions involving the hands, wrists, and arms.
Ability to visually inspect parts, interpret and read blueprints, technical drawings, work instructions, and use gauges, and measuring devices.
Ability to distinguish colors, dimensions, and surface defects when performing quality inspections.
Ability to hear and communicate effectively in a manufacturing environment.
Ability to safely operate equipment in a fast-paced production setting while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, safety shoes, and other equipment as required.
Ability to work in an environment with exposure to machine noise, metal chips, cutting fluids, lubricants, and varying temperatures.
Ability to maintain regular attendance and work scheduled shifts, including overtime as required.
Work Environment
Manufacturing environment with exposure to moving mechanical equipment.
Frequent interaction with machine tools, raw materials, and finished products.
Compliance with all company safety policies, housekeeping requirements, and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention practices.
Required use of appropriate PPE and adherence to all safety procedures.
Essential Functions Disclaimer
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.
About HEICO
Heico has a history of success. Since its founding over 40 years ago The Heico Companies has grown from a single business to over 80 separate companies through a strategic acquisition policy, and by reinvesting its earnings into internal growth and new prospects. Historically talented at restoring distressed companies, Heico now strategically targets acquisitions that will complement its ever-growing portfolio of companies in manufacturing, construction, and industrial services.
These four core operations are organized into groups: Metal Processing Group, Construction Solutions Group, Applied Solutions Group, and Industrial Technologies Group. Once acquired, new Heico companies are assigned to a group and run on a stand-alone basis, allowing for great independence as well as the opportunity to share knowledge about markets, production processes, and management practices across other Heico groups and companies. Each Group has its own corporate team.
Heico continues to seek out new opportunities and maintain its standard of success. The Heico Companies has remained a privately held company since its creation and maintains a majority ownership in each of its operations, which generates more than $3.3 billion dollars in revenues. Many of our businesses are certified Woman-owned Business Enterprises (WBE).
More information about the holding company and overall organization can be found at www.heicocompanies.com.

Quality Business Systems Director
Transform the Future of Quality at DuPont
At DuPont, we are advancing manufacturing and supply chain performance through Operational Excellence, digital enablement, and the DuPont Business System to deliver safer, more reliable, higher-quality outcomes for our customers.
We are seeking a Quality Business Systems Director
to define and scale DuPont’s global manufacturing quality strategy. Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Excellence

This role is ideal for a quality and operational excellence leader who can connect strategy to execution, influence across a matrixed organization, and build a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
What You'll Do
As the Quality Business Systems Director, you will lead a small global team responsible for developing and deploying quality standards, tools, playbooks, metrics, and capability-building programs that improve customer outcomes and operational performance across DuPont.
You will:
Define and deploy DuPont’s global manufacturing quality excellence strategy across businesses and manufacturing sites.
Partner directly with Business Quality Leaders, Business Operational Excellence Directors, Integrated Operations Leaders, and Manufacturing, Engineering, Digital, Automation, and IT leaders to improve end-to-end SQDIP performance.
Develop and continuously improve global quality standards, toolkits, playbooks, training, and communities of practice.
Leverage and integrate artificial intelligence to develop/improve quality management approaches and techniques
Serve as a trusted advisor to business and site leaders by facilitating Kaizen events, problem-solving workshops, and transformation initiatives.
Establish quality performance metrics, analytics, and single sources of truth that enable data-driven decisions from the plant floor to senior leadership.
Integrate quality excellence practices into the DuPont Business System to create a consistent enterprise approach.
Build organizational capability and foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and customer-focused execution.

The Quality Business Systems Director will help shape how DuPont improves quality, reliability, delivery, productivity, and cost across the enterprise.
By working across Operations, Quality, and business leadership, this role will translate business needs into practical standards, capability-building routines, and measurable improvements that strengthen customer confidence and operational performance.

Influence quality performance across multiple global businesses and sites.
Strengthen the relationship between manufacturing quality COE, business quality leadership, and customer outcomes.
Build scalable standards, tools, and routines that support quality aligned to the DuPont Business System.
Develop quality leaders and practitioners through coaching, training, and communities of practice.
Deliver measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, productivity, and cost.

Job Description
Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The World™.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems.

Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location here at our BAE Systems facility in Austin, TX. 100% of the time.

This role drives integrated strategies that elevate safety, quality, cost, and delivery while cultivating a culture of disciplined problem‑solving and operational rigor. The director oversees the development of data‑driven systems and processes that strengthen decision‑making, transparency, and compliance across a 1,000‑person defense manufacturing facility. They collaborate closely with senior leadership and cross‑functional teams to align improvement initiatives with long‑term strategic objectives and customer commitments. Through strong leadership and effective change‑management, the director enables sustainable operational excellence and advances the factory’s mission.


  • Lead Lean Six Sigma and CI initiatives: Kaizen events, 5S, VSM, FMEA, root cause analysis, and other best practices.

  • Shape and execute an industrial engineering strategy that optimizes facility layout, throughput, takt time, labor standards, capacity planning, and simulation modeling.
  • Elevate standardized work, visual management, and digital factory tools to ensure consistency and efficiency.
  • Design and implement training programs on Lean, Six Sigma, CI tools, industrial engineering, and compliance for all levels of the workforce.
  • Establish Lean champions, CI practitioners, and cross-functional improvement teams.
  • Oversee continual upskilling to maintain high standards in process discipline and data-driven thinking.


Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required (Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Business, or related); Master’s or MBA preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 12+ years in industrial/operations leadership in regulated or defense manufacturing environments.
    • Proven execution of CI initiatives with measurable outcomes in cost, quality, and productivity.
    • Demonstrated IE expertise: layout optimization, simulation, takt time, DFMA, and capacity modeling.
    • Strong background in compliance with standards like ITAR, AS9100, DFARS, and internal/external audits.
    • Experience building BI tools, cross-functional dashboards, and applying data insights in operations.


Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
    • Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt (preferred); PMP or similar a plus.
    • Advanced proficiency with data analysis and BI tools.
    • Outstanding leadership, communication, facilitation, and change management skills.
  • Security Requirements:
    • Ability to obtain Secret clearance (or higher).



Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.


About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
Genesis AI
San Carlos, CA
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.
This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.
What You'll Do
Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.
What We're Looking For
You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.
Working conditions
Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.
Why this role
You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.
How We Work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft.
